scope.deltaReview: An independent CORE-53 reviewer read the change after the baseline: ebfb348, 51cf835 and 1a90855, including the new unsafe FFI (csops, the stack-test FFI, the Windows creation attributes and the test FFI). It was a review of the change, not a full audit. It made 4 findings. Three were fixed before the push: the layout of a test structure, the job nesting, and the documentation of with_cleared_stack for foreign exceptions. CI settled the fourth, whether OpenThreadToken works through a handle with THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION: the Windows worker tests that require LowIntegrity passed. A second CORE-53 reviewer read the change of f5e8fc2 and made three low findings, all applied before the commit: a wider pattern for the waiting calls, the search of the source for macOS, and the Linux row of TARGETS.md.
scope.excluded: Upstream crates beyond the calls into them (landlock 0.4.8 read for its write table only).

releaseDecision.reason: Every finding of the four audits is fixed, and CI passed every job at f5e8fc2 (run 45739586059). PASS is not given here: the local AUD-024 checks ran at d54e1db, the release-phase checks run at the tag, and 18 fixes, one of them release-blocking, are shown only by a reading of the diff or by tests that would pass without them. AUD-025, an independent re-audit at the final commit, decides PASS.

grants.grant: Worker setting variable SECRET_PROTECTION_CORE_WORKER
grants.purpose: Tells the child its role and options; on Windows the pipe name and nonce
grants.admits: It stays in the worker's environment; on Linux /proc/PID/environ of a dumpable worker is readable by the user's processes until isolation (the Unix value holds option bits only)
grants.narrowestForm: Remove the variable when serve starts
grants.order: Readable from exec until isolation on Linux

grants.grant: Reply limit `most` on the parent
grants.admits: A worker makes the parent reserve up to `most`, or end the process
grants.narrowestForm: Reserve as bytes arrive, with a fallible allocation
grants.whyNoNarrower: Not taken: documented instead in ebfb348

grants.grant: Startup report and admission
grants.purpose: Admit only a clean worker isolated as required
grants.admits: It trusts the worker's own words
grants.whyNoNarrower: No kernel attestation exists; SECURITY.md states the trust. Since ebfb348 no Linux worker starts where another process of the user may attach

grants.grant: Pages Send and Sync; Region handle
grants.purpose: Move buffers between threads; open and close pages
grants.admits: A Region can change page protections from a shared or stale handle
grants.narrowestForm: unsafe fn, or a Region borrowed from &mut Pages
grants.whyNoNarrower: Not taken: comment corrected in ebfb348

grants.grant: WritableFolder descriptor (O_PATH on Linux)
grants.admits: Nothing beyond what the program holds; macOS grants by path (documented)
grants.whyNoNarrower: Already narrow

grants.grant: Cleared dumpable flag and core limit 0
grants.admits: It does not refuse holders of CAP_SYS_PTRACE in the user namespace the program started in
grants.narrowestForm: Read the start namespace and report Unknown outside the first (ebfb348)

grants.grant: New user, network and IPC namespaces
grants.admits: Every process of the user holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE over the new namespace; only the cleared flag protects
grants.whyNoNarrower: None narrower; the flag is read back before entering

grants.grant: Read-only open of any path
grants.admits: Opens /proc/PID/mem, /proc/PID/fd and /proc/PID/environ of processes the kernel lets it reach
grants.whyNoNarrower: No practical filter rule; documented in ebfb348

grants.grant: Every prctl except the mark, PR_SET_DUMPABLE and PR_SET_PTRACER
grants.admits: PR_SCHED_CORE on other processes

grants.grant: sendto only without an address; sendmsg unless refuse_sendmsg
grants.admits: Addressed datagrams through sendmsg on sockets opened before
grants.whyNoNarrower: Documented in ebfb348

grants.grant: Nine terminal ioctls, and TCFLSH with TCIFLUSH since ebfb348
grants.admits: Settings of any terminal the process holds
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for hidden input; documented

grants.grant: write, ftruncate, sendfile, splice and copy_file_range on descriptors held
grants.admits: Changes files opened for writing before isolation
grants.whyNoNarrower: Documented

grants.grant: Signals to any process unless signals_to_self_only
grants.admits: Any signal to processes of the user

grants.grant: Landlock write rights, TCP bind and connect, abstract-socket and signal scopes, best effort
grants.admits: Reading and executing are not handled
grants.whyNoNarrower: Correct for each ABI; outcomes read back

grants.grant: TSYNC with Options::all_threads
grants.admits: Replaces their own Landlock layers
grants.whyNoNarrower: Documented

grants.grant: Unix launch: environment = setting; descriptors 0 and 1 are socket pairs (Linux) or pipes (macOS); 2 is /dev/null or the terminal; close from 3
grants.admits: The parent's session and controlling terminal until serve calls setsid; the unused direction of each socket
grants.whyNoNarrower: Not taken; recorded as observations

grants.grant: Private-table launcher thread (close_range with UNSHARE and CLOEXEC)
grants.purpose: No inherited descriptors on old glibc
grants.admits: A copy of every parent descriptor until the thread exits
grants.whyNoNarrower: Already narrow

grants.grant: Worker descriptors 0 and 1
grants.admits: Reachable while another process may attach: the start-up window and user-owned namespaces
grants.narrowestForm: No worker start where another process may attach (ebfb348)

grants.grant: Sandbox file-read* except terminal devices
grants.purpose: The program keeps reading its inputs and libraries
grants.admits: Every file the user can read, which a compromised process can send through a kept channel
grants.whyNoNarrower: A library cannot know the program's paths; SECURITY.md does not state what it allows

grants.grant: Own terminal by path: read, data writes, all ioctls
grants.admits: Any bytes and settings changes; TIOCSTI through a controlling terminal

grants.grant: sysctl-read, all
grants.purpose: System libraries read hw.* and kern.*
grants.admits: Every sysctl, other processes' arguments and environment included

grants.grant: PT_DENY_ATTACH, and since 51cf835 the code signature read with csops
grants.admits: PT_DENY_ATTACH alone does not stop task_for_pid
grants.narrowestForm: NoMemoryReading Confirmed only under the hardened runtime without get-task-allow (51cf835)

grants.grant: Folder grants: create, write data and unlink beneath each folder
grants.admits: Rewriting files others put there; case-insensitive siblings (documented)
grants.whyNoNarrower: Narrow as documented; no file-link, so hard links stay refused

grants.grant: Process access list D:P(A;;0x100001;;;OW) since ebfb348 (0x101001 before)
grants.purpose: Owner may wait and end the process
grants.admits: Before ebfb348, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION opened the token

grants.grant: Token object's own access list, unchanged
grants.admits: Any process of the user that holds a handle with the right to open the token may change its default list
grants.whyNoNarrower: The process list no longer gives that right; a protected token list was not added

grants.grant: Start-up default list D:P(A;;0x120800;;;OW)(A;;0x120800;;;<package SID>), set by the parent on the suspended worker (51cf835)
grants.purpose: Close the threads Windows starts before the census, and let the census read them back
grants.admits: The worker's own package reads, waits on and queries its threads
grants.whyNoNarrower: The census needs the package entry to read the lists back
grants.order: none since 51cf835: the worker runs only once the list reads back

grants.grant: Less privileged AppContainer: ALL_APPLICATION_PACKAGES opt-out, no capabilities (51cf835)
grants.admits: Files, registry keys and brokers granted to ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES (S-1-15-2-2), which CI grants on the program folder; a persistent profile folder
grants.whyNoNarrower: The program and its libraries must be readable and runnable by that group

grants.grant: Creation attributes: mitigation policy (extension points off; images neither remote nor low-label; System32 first) and the child-process restriction (51cf835)
grants.admits: None beyond the policies
grants.whyNoNarrower: Set at creation

grants.grant: Job with UI limits, made by the worker itself before its census
grants.admits: The worker's start-up code runs before the job
grants.whyNoNarrower: Windows does not nest a job with UI limits, so one given at creation would fail the start of a launcher that runs in any job

grants.grant: DETACHED_PROCESS since 51cf835 (CREATE_NO_WINDOW before)
grants.admits: None: the worker has no console
grants.whyNoNarrower: Already narrow

grants.grant: Named pipe: one instance, first-instance flag, remote clients rejected, user and package SID entries; client PID and 128-bit nonce
grants.purpose: The worker connects to its launcher
grants.admits: Any process of the user may connect first; repeated contention stops a start (AUD-009-SEC003, accepted)
grants.whyNoNarrower: The user entry is needed by the AppContainer check

grants.grant: Parent's full handles from CreateProcessW, held while the worker is suspended
grants.purpose: Set the start-up list, then resume or end the worker
grants.admits: Held until resume, then exchanged for wait and terminate rights (tested)
grants.whyNoNarrower: Already narrow

findings.title: From exec until its isolation a Linux worker is dumpable, so another process of the user could take its channel while it starts.
findings.verifiedWhere: Run 45736641331 at 1a90855: 'no worker starts while any process of the user may attach', in the checks job's step with Yama's ptrace_scope at 0
findings.note: d54e1db only downgraded NoMemoryReading; ebfb348 starts no worker where another process of the user may attach.
findings.expected: Protect a worker channel to the degree promised for a protected parent, through startup and admission.
findings.observed: From exec until its isolation a Linux worker is dumpable, so another process of the user could take its channel while it starts.
findings.impact: On affected Linux host policies, confidentiality and integrity of later worker traffic cannot be promised even if the parent was already protected. The prerequisite and short window limit exposure. The isolation guarantee makes this a release blocker.
findings.requiredVerification: None left beyond the recorded verification.

findings.title: Where the Linux start-up window was open (Yama 0), the parent downgraded only NoMemoryReading and still trusted the rest of a report another process could have written, then sent requests.
findings.evidenceBasis: AUD-023 source review; reasoned in the AUD-024 notes (UL-2)
findings.verifiedWhere: Run 45736641331 at 1a90855: 'no worker starts while any process of the user may attach', in the checks job's step with Yama's ptrace_scope at 0
findings.reproduction: Defensive source review and contract comparison.
findings.expected: The parent fails admission when it cannot confirm the startup report and each required worker protection.
findings.observed: Where the Linux start-up window was open (Yama 0), the parent downgraded only NoMemoryReading and still trusted the rest of a report another process could have written, then sent requests.
findings.impact: A caller requiring egress or file restrictions can still receive a worker as admitted when those claims came through a channel whose integrity was unverified. The strict NoMemoryReading regression passes under the permissive policy, and the other admission claims remain exposed.
findings.requiredVerification: None left beyond the recorded verification.

findings.title: A worker's announced reply length makes the parent reserve up to `most` bytes before any arrive, and end the process when the system refuses.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: AUD-024 rule: low findings and non-SEC findings do not block.
findings.verifiedWhere: ebfb348 diff: Worker::call documents `most` as the memory a worker may make the parent take
findings.note: Fixed in the documentation only: the parent still reserves before the bytes arrive.
findings.reproduction: AUD-024 reader notes (P-01): reproduced with a hostile-worker probe
findings.expected: Sizes an attacker controls go through a fallible reservation (CHECK-API-005), and the bound of call_within holds on every path.
findings.observed: A worker's announced reply length makes the parent reserve up to `most` bytes before any arrive, and end the process when the system refuses.
findings.impact: A broken or compromised worker makes the parent commit up to `most` bytes (527 MB measured for 512 MiB announced and 7 bytes sent), or ends it with SIGABRT when the reservation is refused, skipping every Drop. Needs a large `most`.
findings.requiredVerification: None left beyond the recorded verification.

findings.title: In a user namespace its user owns, Linux reported NoMemoryReading Confirmed while any process of the user could attach, read memory and take the worker's channel.

findings.reproduction: AUD-024 reader notes (UL-1): reproduced with unshare -U on Linux 7.0
findings.expected: A protection reported Confirmed holds against new access by another process of the same user (src/protect.rs:264, SECURITY.md:19).

findings.impact: In a user namespace the user owns, with the PID namespace shared, any process of the user read a work area, took the worker's descriptors and returned a forged reply through call_within (synthetic probe on Linux 7.0).

findings.title: The Linux filter allowed prctl(PR_SCHED_CORE) on other processes and read-only opens of /proc/PID/mem, while the docs said calls acting on other processes were limited.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: AUD-024 rule: low findings and non-SEC findings do not block.
findings.evidenceBasis: reproduced at the kernel level, without the crate's filter
findings.verifiedWhere: Run 45736641331 at 1a90855: 'an isolated thread is refused what the filter names and keeps what it needs', which now lists PR_SCHED_CORE (Linux x86-64 and ARM64)
findings.note: The /proc reads stay open as far as the kernel allows them; docs/TECHNICAL.md now says so.
findings.reproduction: AUD-024 reader notes (UL-3): reproduced at the kernel level, without the crate's filter

findings.observed: The Linux filter allowed prctl(PR_SCHED_CORE) on other processes and read-only opens of /proc/PID/mem, while the docs said calls acting on other processes were limited.
findings.impact: An isolated process could change another process's core-scheduling cookie, and read the memory of processes the kernel lets it attach to through /proc/PID/mem.

KeystrokeBytes is built on the stack and copied by each move; only its last place is wiped (Keystroke itself is documented as unwiped).
On the 32-bit test targets, folder.rs binds the non-LFS stat and readdir calls: inode numbers of 2^32 or more fail closed with EOVERFLOW.
A Linux worker keeps the parent's session and controlling terminal from exec until serve calls setsid; POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID would remove that start-up window.
Hypothesis not run: with SIGPIPE at its default, a worker that ends while the parent writes would kill the parent instead of returning BrokenPipe.
On non-pty terminals Linux TCSETSF waits for output between its flush and its set (from kernel source, not run); this is the class of AUD-023-FUN001.
The macOS sandbox allows every sysctl read, including other processes' arguments and environment, and SECURITY.md does not say what file-read* lets a compromised process read and send.
